questions.question: How can you determine if the wood is dry before you inspect a wood aircraft airframe?
questions.idealAnswer: A moisture meter should be used to verify the percentage of moisture in the structure.

questions.question: What effect does moisture/ humidity have on wood?
questions.idealAnswer: Moisture and humidity causes wood to swell.

questions.question: Name one characteristic all aircraft approved wood species have in common?
questions.idealAnswer: The slope of the grain cannot be steeper than 1:15.

questions.question: For wood to be certificated for aircraft usage, what must it have?
questions.idealAnswer: The wood should have traceability to the source that can provide certification to a military specification (MIL -SPEC).

questions.question: Which wood is the standard for comparisons in aircraft structures?
questions.idealAnswer: Spruce is the standard to witch all other woods are Measured.

questions.question: Can Northern White pine be substituted for Spruce in an aircraft structure?
questions.idealAnswer: No, Northern White pine is weaker in comparison and an increase in size must be calculated to substitute for spruce.

concepts.label: Northern White pine is weaker in comparison
terms: northern white pine is weaker in comparison

concepts.label: an increase in size must be calculated to substitute for spruce
terms: an increase in size must be calculated to substitute for spruce

questions.question: When would mineral streaks cause a piece of aircraft quality wood to be rejected?
questions.idealAnswer: Mineral Streaks-- Unacceptable when accompanied by decay.

questions.question: When are pine knot clusters acceptable in a piece of aircraft quality wood?
questions.idealAnswer: Only if the produce a small effect on grain direction.

questions.question: Are hard knots acceptable in a piece of aircraft quality wood?
questions.idealAnswer: Hard knots are unacceptable.

questions.question: What does a metal bushing do in a wood structure?
questions.idealAnswer: Protects the wood structure.

questions.question: What type of wood should be used for structural repairs in aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: Soft wood.

questions.question: What kind of wood is used in aircraft besides solid wood?
questions.idealAnswer: Plywood or Laminate.

questions.question: Are pin knot clusters allowable in aircraft structural wood?
questions.idealAnswer: Yes, if they cause only a small effect on grain direction

concepts.label: if they cause only a small effect on grain direction
terms: if they cause only a small effect on grain direction

questions.question: What does "pot-life" mean?
questions.idealAnswer: The length of time a resin will remain workable after the catalyst has been added.

questions.question: Why is the scarf joint angle and condition of a wood spar repair important?
questions.idealAnswer: Strength of the repair (more gluing surface area= stronger repair.) The spar is the most important structure of the wing, and takes on most of the loads in flight.

concepts.label: Strength of the repair The spar is the most important structure of the wing
terms: strength of the repair the spar is the most important structure of the wing

concepts.label: takes on most of the loads in flight
terms: takes on most of the loads in flight

questions.question: What kind of glue is recommended for making a repair to wooden aircraft structure?
questions.idealAnswer: Synthetic resin glue is used.

questions.question: How is pressure applied to the glued joint when splicing a wooden aircraft wing spar?
questions.idealAnswer: Parallel clamps are used to apply pressure.

questions.question: What is the correct repair to a wooden wing spar if wing attach bolt holes in the spar are elongated?
questions.idealAnswer: Splice in a new section of spar, and drill new holes, or replace the spar.

concepts.label: Splice in a new section of spar
terms: splice in a new section of spar

questions.question: What kind of repair is recommended for a hole in the plywood skin of an aircraft wing?
questions.idealAnswer: A scarf patch.

questions.question: What is the recommended taper for a splayed patch in plywood aircraft skin?
questions.idealAnswer: The taper for a splayed patch is 5:1 (5x the thickness of the plywood skin.)

questions.question: What is the recommended taper for a scarf patch in plywood aircraft skin?
questions.idealAnswer: The taper is 12:1 (12x thickness if the skin.)

questions.question: Why should sandpaper never be used when preparing a scarf joint in a wing spar for splicing?
questions.idealAnswer: Dust caused by sanding will plug pores of wood and glue will not form a good bond.

concepts.label: Dust caused by sanding will plug pores of wood
terms: dust caused by sanding will plug pores of wood

concepts.label: glue will not form a good bond
terms: glue will not form a good bond

questions.question: What is the largest hole in a plywood wing skin that can be repaired with a fabric patch?
questions.idealAnswer: One inch diameter

questions.question: How long should a glue joint be kept under pressure when splicing a wooden wing spar?
questions.idealAnswer: At least 7 hours.

questions.question: Are mineral streaks in a piece of structural aircraft wood cause for rejection?
questions.idealAnswer: No, as long as no decay is present.

concepts.label: as long as no decay is present
terms: as long as no decay is present

questions.question: Which area of a wooden aircraft wing spar cannot contain a splice?
questions.idealAnswer: Under wing-attachment, landing gear, engine mount, lift, or interplane strut fittings.

questions.question: What is done to a splice in a wooden wing spar to strengthen the splice?
questions.idealAnswer: Glue reinforcing plates to both sides of the splice.

questions.question: Why must abrupt changes in cross sectional area of a wooden structural member be avoided?
questions.idealAnswer: They can concentrate stresses and cause failure.

questions.question: What are the three forms of wood commonly used in aircraft construction?
questions.idealAnswer: Solid, laminated, and plywood.

questions.question: What type of wood should be used when splicing or reinforcing plywood webs? The same type as the original plywood.
questions.idealAnswer: The same type as the original plywood.

questions.question: Name at least four distinct kinds of defects found in wood.
questions.idealAnswer: Decay, dry-rot, knots, splits, pitch pockets, cross grain, curly grain, and checks.

questions.question: Can a section of wood containing a hard knot be used?
questions.idealAnswer: Yes. Within specified limits. Only (hard tight knots) that do not disturb the grain more than 1 inch over 15 inches 15:1 can be used.

questions.question: Is compression wood acceptable for structural repairs?
questions.idealAnswer: No , it can never be used. Compression wood shrinks more easily and can cause warping, twisting and distortion.

concepts.label: it can never be used. Compression wood shrinks more easily
terms: it can never be used. compression wood shrinks more easily

questions.question: Why should various pieces of wood being joined be kept in the same room for at least 24 hours prior to joining?
questions.idealAnswer: It allows moisture content to equalize. This minimizes dimensional changes in the wood.

questions.question: Why is it important to consider the open-assembly time when gluing wooden structures?
questions.idealAnswer: If you exceed open-assembly time, the glue might begin to set before the joint is assembled, which might cause the joint to fail.

concepts.label: the glue might begin to set before the joint is assembled
terms: the glue might begin to set before the joint is assembled

concepts.label: which might cause the joint to fail
terms: which might cause the joint to fail

questions.question: Why is it important to apply proper clamping pressure to a glue joint?
questions.idealAnswer: Clamping forces the air out of the joint and brings the surfaces together evenly, which promotes glue strength.

concepts.label: Clamping forces the air out of the joint
terms: clamping forces the air out of the joint

questions.question: Describe some of the methods used to apply pressure to glue joints.
questions.idealAnswer: Clamps, nailing strips, power presses, brads, nails, and small screws.

questions.question: What type of glue might have been used in older wooden aircraft which requires careful inspection to check for deterioration?
questions.idealAnswer: Casein glue.

questions.question: What are the three types of glues used in modern aircraft construction and repair?
questions.idealAnswer: Resorcinol glue. Phenol formaldehyde glue. Epoxy resin glue.

questions.question: What minimum curing temperature should be observed when joining wood with adhesives?
questions.idealAnswer: Whatever is specified by the glue manufacturer, usually 70°F.

concepts.label: Whatever is specified by the glue manufacturer
terms: whatever is specified by the glue manufacturer

questions.question: Whenever inspecting wood structures, why might it be important to consider stains and discolored areas?
questions.idealAnswer: Stains and discoloration are signs that decay may be present.

concepts.label: discoloration are signs that decay may be present
terms: discoloration are signs that decay may be present

questions.question: What type of joint is used to splice a solid or rectangular wood spar?
questions.idealAnswer: A scarf joint is used.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of splices allowed for any single spar?
questions.idealAnswer: Two is the maximum number of splices in a spar.

questions.question: Describe the characteristics of a scarf joint.
questions.idealAnswer: T wo pieces joined together, tapered, or beveled on a slope of 12:1

concepts.label: or beveled on a slope of 12:1
terms: or beveled on a slope of 12:1

questions.question: Why must the beveled cut be accurate on both pieces of wood being repaired with a scarf joint?
questions.idealAnswer: They need to match to ensure a tight glue joint.

questions.question: What are the two primary uses for plywood and aircraft construction?
questions.idealAnswer: Reinforcing plates (gussets) and aircraft skin.

questions.question: Give at least three examples of the types of plywood skin repairs.
questions.idealAnswer: Scarf patches, splayed patches, surface patches, and plug patches.

questions.question: What should be done to prevent a plywood patch and the pressure plate from sticking together if glue is extruded from the joint?
questions.idealAnswer: The use of waxed paper or vinyl plastic between the patch and the pressure plate.

concepts.label: The use of waxed paper or vinyl plastic between the patch
terms: the use of waxed paper or vinyl plastic between the patch

questions.question: What is the purpose of large surface area washers when used on wooden structures?
questions.idealAnswer: Large washers provide an additional bearing area for the hardware to prevent damage to the wood when hardware is tightened.

questions.question: Name two methods for repairing plywood skin.
questions.idealAnswer: Fabric, splayed, surface, plug, or scarf.
